Three (or more) points are collinear if a straight line passes through all points.

With that in mind, let's examine our diagrams in turn.

- Statement I is true. There is a straight line that passes through these three points.

- Statement II is true. We can't draw a straight line that passes through these three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/2c20ebe076b3e655b7709ccb337c68d4aa8505bfabdb5a8755e5a1410642d612.png)

- Statement III is false. We can't draw a straight line that passes through these three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/9859ea0144923d69e37d64130910608f6fc3e7afe09d74af19a5402030e0d3cb.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
html:
Three (or more) points are collinear if a straight line passes through all points.

With that in mind, let's examine our diagrams in turn.

  • Statement I is true. There is a straight line that passes through these three points.
  • Statement II is true. We can't draw a straight line that passes through these three points.
  • Statement III is false. We can't draw a straight line that passes through these three points.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
